message: No detected untrusted source handling: The code runs 'dvc pull' to fetch data from a remote source (S3) but performs no checksum verification, signature validation, or pinned revision check on the retrieved artifacts.
No detected label flipping detection: No code validates label values against an expected set, compares label distributions, or uses any label-noise detection tool before or during training.

No detected data poisoning defenses: The data preparation pipeline applies only standard one-hot encoding and label binarization with no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious inputs.

No detected model integrity verification: The code loads the model and encoder/lb objects via joblib.load() with no hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision; it simply loads from a file path without any integrity validation.
No detected label distribution validation: No code checks class balance, expected label set, or anomalous sample distribution before training begins.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no trigger detection, activation analysis, or gradient anomaly detection anywhere in the training pipeline.
No detected differential privacy: The code uses a standard sklearn RandomForestClassifier with GridSearchCV and no differential privacy library or mechanism is applied.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness testing libraries or techniques (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD, etc.) are used anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: While a train/test split is performed, there is no hashing, signing, or isolation mechanism to prevent metric manipulation; the test set is accessible throughout and results are only printed without any integrity protection.
No detected output bounds checks: The predict_salary endpoint returns the raw model prediction with no NaN guards, bounds checks, or sanity validation on the output.
No detected prompt injection defenses: This is a tabular classification model (RandomForest), not an LLM, so prompt-injection defenses are not applicable.
